title: Why a logo is the smallest part of an identity
excerpt: A mark is where an identity begins. Everything it has to live on is where it succeeds or fails.
body:
People judge an identity by its logo because it’s the one thing they can point at. But a logo is a single asset inside a system, and the system does most of the work: type, colour, layout, imagery, tone of voice, the way a pack is built and a page is spaced.

A strong mark in a weak system looks borrowed. A modest mark in a strong system looks inevitable. The difference is whether anyone has decided how the brand behaves when the logo isn’t there.

That’s why we often design the mark last. We want to know what the brand sounds like, what it does with space, and which two or three rules will keep it recognisable on a shelf, a screen and a shipping box.

Here’s a simple test for any identity: cover the logo. If you still know whose it is, the system is working.
